medium.note: Meta through Muse: the most reliable builder (#305), first among the medium models.
ChatGPT through Codex, on GPT-5.6 Sol: medium again since 2026-10-20 (weak from 2026-10-11, on Terra), after agy and before Sonnet.
Claude Sonnet at xhigh (#317 part 5): a medium seat on every Claude account, which switches between it and Opus as the work needs (work.Worker._switch).

strong.note: Claude Opus, on every Claude account, beside its Sonnet.

claude-1.note: The Claude subscription the bot has always used; shared with its owner and bright-bots-harness. Second in the usage order: Opus for strong roles, Sonnet (medium) for easy and medium builds, and each run switches between the two as the work needs. One lane, so it works one item at a time (#695).

claude-2.note: A second Claude account, capped at 90% of both its 5-hour session and its week. Kept back for planning and adversarial review on Opus: after the medium models in the usage order, and it builds only when no other subscription that may is free (build_last), on Sonnet unless the item is hard; its runs switch between the two as the work needs. One lane, so it works one item at a time (#695).

claude-3.note: A third Claude account, the bot's own: any hour, no caps. First in the usage order: Opus for strong roles, Sonnet (medium) for easy and medium builds, and each run switches between the two as the work needs. Two lanes, so it works two items at once.

claude-4.note: A fourth Claude account (token added 2026-10-04) with no weekly cap: any hour under 50% of its 5-hour session (off_hours), and from 03:00 to 15:00 Central (its window) up to 70% of it. Opus for strong roles, Sonnet (medium) for easy and medium builds, and each run switches between the two as the work needs.

claude-5.note: A fifth Claude account (token added 2026-10-04): any hour, capped at 40% of its 5-hour session and 60% of its week, and from Sunday 17:00 Central until its week resets (Monday at 09:00 UTC, 03:00 Central in winter) at 80% of its 5-hour session and all of its week, with its session's last hour too (`late_week`): its only time past those caps. Opus for strong roles, Sonnet (medium) for easy and medium builds, and each run switches between the two as the work needs.

claude-6.note: A sixth Claude account (token added 2026-10-05), same rules as claude-4 with no weekly cap: any hour under 50% of its 5-hour session (off_hours), and from 03:00 to 15:00 Central (its window) up to 70% of it. Opus for strong roles, Sonnet (medium) for easy and medium builds, and each run switches between the two as the work needs.

claude-7.note: A seventh Claude account (token added 2026-10-07) with no weekly cap: any hour under 50% of its 5-hour session (off_hours), and from 01:00 to 10:00 Central (its window) up to 70% of it. Second in the usage order, after claude-3: Opus for strong roles, Sonnet (medium) for easy and medium builds, and each run switches between the two as the work needs.

claude-8.note: An eighth Claude account (token added 2026-10-23): any hour, capped at 85% of its 5-hour session with no weekly cap. Third in the usage order, after claude-3 and claude-7: Opus for strong roles, Sonnet (medium) for easy and medium builds, and each run switches between the two as the work needs. Two lanes (three on 2026-10-27, #2112; two since #2129), so it works up to two items at once: each run takes its own reading before it starts and watches it during every call, so they pass its cap by at most one reading's worth.

gpt.note: ChatGPT through the Codex CLI, logged in on the machine as agent-gpt (`codex login`). GPT-5.6 Sol, its top tier, since 2026-10-20, and medium again with it: weak from 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-20, on Terra, when it built easy items only (#682).

agy.note: Google's Antigravity CLI, logged in on the machine as agent-agy. Gemini 3.8 Flash (High); `agy models` lists the names, each carrying its effort. Its usage is its own `agy -p /usage` (no model call), the Gemini pool's row: read before the run, after every call and every ten minutes during one.

muse.note: Meta's Muse Code CLI, logged in on both boxes as agent-muse (`muse login`). Its usage is the TUI's `/usage` panel (`muse exec` runs no slash commands), read before the run, after every call and every ten minutes during one. Four lanes of its own (two since #1273), under the one login: its caps are its whole plan, which read under 10% of the week on one lane, so the one run at a time of a capped subscription (#695) bought it nothing. Each box runs three jobs at most, set for m7i-flex.xlarge (4 vCPUs, 16 GB), though both are still m7i-flex.large (2 vCPUs, 8 GB), the largest the Free plan allows, and lean on compressed swap in memory (reviews/2026-10-27-muse-usage.md, finding 4): one of Muse's own runners is on the night box (`night-vm-muse`) and three on the Muse box (`night-vm-muse-b2`, `-2-b2`, `-3-b2`). It also fills gpt's and agy's lanes on the night box while one of them cannot start work (`fill_in`: capped, off, outside its hours, backing off), on its two runners there, `night-vm-muse-fill` and `night-vm-muse-fill-2`; the three share those two lanes. So Muse runs six at most, and the boxes six jobs together (`machine_parallel`; bot/machine/README.md, The Muse box). On Meta's $50 plan since 2026-10-11, four times the usage of the one before; its caps are shares of whatever the plan gives, so they stretch with it. Its week has no start headroom (`start_headroom`, #682): a build or a plan may start right up to the 100% cap, since a run the cap cuts off keeps its work and Muse then waits for the reset.
